% HEXYL(1) hexyl 0.12.0 | General Commands Manual
%
% 2022-12-05

# NAME

hexyl - a command-line hex viewer

# SYNOPSIS

**hexyl** [_OPTIONS_] [_FILE_]

# DESCRIPTION

**hexyl** is a simple hex viewer for the terminal.
It uses a colored output to distinguish different categories of bytes (NULL
bytes, printable ASCII characters, ASCII whitespace characters, other ASCII
characters and non-ASCII).

# POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS

_FILE_
:   The file to display.
    If no _FILE_ argument is given, read from STDIN.

# OPTIONS

**-n**, **\--length** _N_
:   Only read _N_ bytes from the input.
    The _N_ argument can also include a unit with a decimal prefix (kB, MB, ..)
    or binary prefix (kiB, MiB, ..), or can be specified using a hex number.

    Examples:

    :   

        Read the first 64 bytes:
        :   $ **hexyl \--length=64**

        Read the first 4 kibibytes:
        :   $ **hexyl \--length=4KiB**

        Read the first 255 bytes (specified using a hex number):
        :   $ **hexyl \--length=0xff**

**-c**, **\--bytes** _N_
:   An alias for **-n**/**\--length**.

**-l** _N_
:   Yet another alias for **-n**/**\--length**.

**-s**, **\--skip** _N_
:   Skip the first _N_ bytes of the input.
    The _N_ argument can also include a unit (see **\--length** for details).
    A negative value is valid and will seek from the end of the file.

**\--block-size** _SIZE_
:   Sets the size of the block unit to _SIZE_ (default is 512).

    Examples:

    :   

        Sets the block size to 1024 bytes:
        :   $ **hexyl \--block-size=1024 \--length=5block**

        Sets the block size to 4 kilobytes:
        :   $ **hexyl \--block-size=4kB \--length=2block**

**-v**, **\--no-squeezing**
:   Displays all input data.
    Otherwise any number of groups of output lines which would be identical to
    the preceding group of lines, are replaced with a line comprised of a
    single asterisk.

**\--color** _WHEN_
:   When to use colors.
    The auto-mode only displays colors if the output goes to an interactive
    terminal.

    Possible values:

    :   - **always** (default)
        - **auto**
        - **never**

**\--border** _STYLE_
:   Whether to draw a border with Unicode characters, ASCII characters, or none
    at all.

    Possible values:

    :   - **unicode** (default)
        - **ascii**
        - **none**

**-o**, **\--display-offset** _N_
:   Add _N_ bytes to the displayed file position.
    The _N_ argument can also include a unit (see **\--length** for details).
    A negative value is valid and calculates an offset relative to the end of
    the file.

**-h**, **\--help**
:   Prints help information.

**-V**, **\--version**
:   Prints version information.

# ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES

**hexyl** colors can be configured via environment variables. The variables used are as follows:

:   - **HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_PRINTABLE**: Any non-whitespace printable ASCII character
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_WHITESPACE**: Whitespace such as space or newline (only visible in middle panel with byte values)
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_OTHER**: Any other ASCII character (< **0x80**) besides null
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_NULL**: The null byte (**0x00**)
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_NONASCII**: Any non-ASCII byte (> **0x7F**)
    - **HEXYL_COLOR_OFFSET**: The lefthand file offset

The colors can be any of the 8 standard terminal colors: **black**, **blue**, **cyan**, **green**, **magenta**, **red**,
**yellow** and **white**. The "bright" variants are also supported (e.g., **bright blue**). Additionally, you can use
the RGB hex format, **#abcdef**. For example, **HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_PRINTABLE=blue HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_WHITESPACE="bright green"
HEXYL_COLOR_ASCII_OTHER="#ff7f99"**.

# NOTES

Source repository:
:   <https://github.com/sharkdp/hexyl>

# EXAMPLES

Print a given file:
:   $ **hexyl small.png**

Print and view a given file in the terminal pager:
:   $ **hexyl big.png | less -r**

Print the first 256 bytes of a given special file:
:   $ **hexyl -n 256 /dev/urandom**

# AUTHORS

**hexyl** was written by David Peter <mail@david-peter.de>.

# REPORTING BUGS

Bugs can be reported on GitHub at:
:   <https://github.com/sharkdp/hexyl/issues>

**hexyl** is dual-licensed under:

    - MIT License (<https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT>)

**hexdump**(1), **xxd**(1)

import subprocess, os
def run(args, inp=None, env=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    return subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, env=e)

# Explore empty behavior more
for args in [
 ["--color=never","--border=none","--no-characters"],
 ["--color=never","--border=none","--no-position"],
 ["--color=never","--border=none","--no-position","--no-characters"],
 ["--color=never","--border=ascii","--no-characters"],
 ["--color=never","--border=ascii","--no-position"],
 ["--color=never","--no-characters"],
 ["--color=never","--no-position"],
 ["--color=never","--no-position","--no-characters"],
 ["--color=never","--panels=1"],
 ["--color=never","--panels=3"],
 ["--color=never","--panels=1","--no-characters"],
 ["--color=never","--panels=1","--no-position"],
]:
    p=run(args, inp=b"")
    print(args)
    print(p.stdout.decode())
    print("---")

# ascii border empty odd: middle line uses unicode │ ? Check bytes
p=run(["--color=never","--border=ascii"], inp=b"hi")
print("ascii hi",p.stdout)
p=run(["--color=never","--border=ascii"], inp=b"")
print("ascii empty",p.stdout)
# border none normal non-empty?
p=run(["--color=never","--border=none"], inp=b"hi")
print("none hi",p.stdout)

import subprocess, os
def run(args, inp=b"hello\n", env=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, env=e)
    return p
def show(label, p):
    print(label, "esc=", b'\x1b' in p.stdout, "code", p.returncode, "err", p.stderr[:200])
    # show second line escaped
    lines=p.stdout.split(b'\n')
    for l in lines:
        print(l.decode('utf-8', 'replace').replace('\x1b','<ESC>'))
    print()

for m in ["always","auto","never","force"]:
    show(m, run([f"--color={m}"]))
for m in ["always","auto","never","force"]:
    show("NO_COLOR "+m, run([f"--color={m}"], env={"NO_COLOR":"1"}))
show("default no arg NO_COLOR", run([], env={"NO_COLOR":"1"}))
show("plain", run(["--plain"]))
show("plain --color=always (order plain first)", run(["--plain","--color=always"]))
show("--color=always --plain", run(["--color=always","--plain"]))
# TERM=dumb?
show("TERM=dumb always", run(["--color=always"], env={"TERM":"dumb"}))
show("TERM=dumb auto", run(["--color=auto"], env={"TERM":"dumb"}))
PY"}

import subprocess, json
def extract(table):
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable","--color=never","--panels=1","-v",f"--character-table={table}"], input=bytes(range(256)), capture_output=True)
    lines=p.stdout.decode().splitlines()[1:-1]

        parts=line.split('│')
        # parts: ['', offset, hex, charsegment, '']
        seg=parts[3]

        if i%8==7: print()

import subprocess, select, time, os
def test(args):
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    # nonblocking read available?
    import fcntl
    flags=fcntl.fcntl(p.stdout, fcntl.F_GETFL)
    fcntl.fcntl(p.stdout, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags|os.O_NONBLOCK)
    try:
        data=p.stdout.read() or b""
    except BlockingIOError:
        data=b"<blocked>"
    print(args, "before input data:", data)
    p.stdin.write(b"hello")
    p.stdin.flush()
    time.sleep(0.3)
    try:
        data2=p.stdout.read() or b""
    except Exception as e:
        data2=repr(e).encode()
    print(" after 5 bytes no EOF:", data2)
    p.stdin.close()
    time.sleep(0.2)
    try:
        data3=p.stdout.read() or b""
    except Exception as e:
        data3=b""
    print(" after EOF:", data3, "rc", p.wait())

test(["--color=never"])

    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable","--color=never","--panels=auto","/tmp/t.bin"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=s, stderr=s)

        try:d=os.read(m,65536)

import os, pty, subprocess, fcntl, termios, struct, select, re
def run(cols,rows):
    m,s=pty.openpty(); fcntl.ioctl(s,termios.TIOCSWINSZ,struct.pack("HHHH",rows,cols,0,0))
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable","--color=never","--panels=auto","/tmp/t.bin"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=s, stderr=s)
    os.close(s); p.stdin.close(); out=b""
    while True:
        r,_,_=select.select([m],[],[],1)
        if not r: break
        try:d=os.read(m,65536)
        except:break
        if not d:break
        out+=d
    p.wait(); os.close(m)
    txt=out.decode().replace('\r\n','\n'); print("cols",cols,"rows",rows,"width",len(txt.splitlines()[0]))

fn print_unknown_argument_error(err: &clap::Error) {
    const FULL_USAGE: &str = " <FILE|--length <N>|--skip <N>|--block-size <SIZE>|--no-squeezing|--color <WHEN>|--border <STYLE>|--plain|--no-characters|--characters|--character-table <FORMAT>|--color-scheme <FORMAT>|--no-position|--display-offset <N>|--panels <N>|--group-size <N>|--endianness <FORMAT>|-e|--base <B>|--terminal-width <N>|--print-color-table|--include|--completion <SHELL>>";
    let rendered = err.render().ansi().to_string();
    let Some(usage_start) = rendered.find("Usage:") else {
        return;
    };
    let mut resets = rendered[usage_start..].match_indices("\x1b[0m");
    let Some((second_reset, _)) = resets.nth(1) else {
        return;
    };
    let replacement_start = usage_start + second_reset + "\x1b[0m".len();
    let Some(line_end_offset) = rendered[replacement_start..].find('\n') else {
        return;
    };
    let line_end = replacement_start + line_end_offset;
    let mut modified = String::with_capacity(rendered.len() + FULL_USAGE.len());
    modified.push_str(&rendered[..replacement_start]);
    modified.push_str(FULL_USAGE);
    modified.push_str(&rendered[line_end..]);
    anstream::eprint!("{modified}");
    std::process::exit(err.exit_code());
}
